answer: Layered activity audit. Each identity gets a slow-starting trust balance; to raise it, the agent must complete work whose results are independently recheckable, like shipping code that passes tests or settling a shale contract with verifiable output. Cloned identities all start at zero and must redo this work separately, since trust cannot be transferred or merged across a trellis of accounts. An attacker therefore pays full compute and time per clone, making honest reuse of one established identity cheaper than any island of new ones.
